paper_type_evidence.quote: We present Atacama Large Millimeter/sub-millimeter Array Cycle 1 observations of the HH 46/47 molecular outflow using combined 12m array and Atacama Compact Array observations.

question.value: How much mass, momentum and energy does the HH 46/47 outflow carry once CO optical depth is corrected, how is it entrained, and can it disperse its parent core?

evidence.quote: We use $^{13}\mbox{CO}$ (1-0) and $\mbox{C}^{18}\mbox{O}$ (1-0) emission to correct for the $^{12}\mbox{CO}$ (1-0) optical depth to accurately estimate the outflow mass, momentum and kinetic energy.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA #2012.1.00382.S.
Two different correlator configurations were used to provide images on six molecular lines and two 2 GHz-wide continuum bands in Band 3.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Config 1: 12CO 0.2 km/s channels, C17O 0.1 km/s, continuum 100.7 and 102.7 GHz; Config 2: 13CO, C18O, CS, C34S at 0.1 km/s

evidence.quote: The continuum emission was observed with two 1875 MHz-wide bands.
Each line was observed with a channel width of 30.5 kHz ($0.1~\mbox{km s}^{-1}$)
CS (2-1) at 97.98 GHz, and $\mbox{C}^{34}\mbox{S}$ (2-1) at 96.41 GHz
Data from both the 12m array and the ACA (including the 7m array and the 12m total power dishes) were obtained.
The combined interferometric data have projected baselines ranging from 7 to 525 m for $^{12}\mbox{CO}$ and $\mbox{C}^{17}\mbox{O}$

The resulting synthesized beam is $1.3\ensuremath{''} \times 1.3\ensuremath{''}$ for the $^{12}\mbox{CO}$ data cube and $3.2\ensuremath{''} \times 1.6\ensuremath{''}$ for the $^{13}\mbox{CO}$ and $\mbox{C}^{18}\mbox{O}$ data cubes.
The observations were carried out using ALMA from November 5, 2013 to April 11, 2015.

assumptions.value: Tdust 30 K, gas-to-dust 100, beta=1, kappa(3mm)=0.9 cm2/g

evidence.quote: assuming a dust temperature of 30 K, a gas-to-dust mass ratio of 100, and an emissivity spectral index ($\beta$) of 1.

method.value: Intensity ratios 13CO/C18O and 12CO/13CO per channel (pixels >5 sigma), weighted mean, parabola fit

evidence.quote: we fit a parabola to the measured intensity ratios with the minimum point fixed at zero velocity

assumptions.value: Same Tex and beam filling factor for all isotopologues, C18O optically thin, LTE

evidence.quote: have the same excitation temperature $T_{\mathrm{ex}}$ and beam filling factor, and that $\mbox{C}^{18}\mbox{O}$ is optically thin

fitting.value: Weighted parabola fit, weights inverse square of uncertainties

evidence.quote: The weights are inversely proportional to the square of the uncertainties of the pixel intensity ratios.
with a reduced $\chi^2$ of 0.22.

method.value: LTE column density per channel with opacity correction; velocity cuts exclude cloud; max column density chosen where several isotopologues detected

evidence.quote: At the pixels where more than one CO isotopologues are detected, we choose the highest column density calculated from these CO isotopologues.

evidence.quote: we will calculate the mass and other properties of the outflow using two typical values of $T_{\mathrm{ex}}$, 15 K and 50 K.

evidence.quote: We adopt an abundance of $^{12}\mbox{CO}$ of $10^{-4}$ relative to $\mbox{H}_2$, and a gas mass of $2.34 \times 10^{-24}$ g per $\mbox{H}_2$ molecules.

findings_qualitative.value: Opacity correction raises 12CO mass, momentum, energy by 8.5, 4.9, 2.4; 13CO/C18O add a further factor 3 in mass

evidence.quote: Correcting for the $^{12}\mbox{CO}$ optical depth increases the estimated mass of the outflow by a factor of 8.5, the momentum by a factor of 4.9, and the kinetic energy by a factor of 2.4.

claims.hypothesis: Optical depth and dense low-velocity gas were underestimated in earlier outflow budgets
claims.experiment: Used 13CO and C18O to correct 12CO opacity and add low-velocity gas
claims.result: Mass up by 8.5x, then a further 3x for red lobe; total 1.6 Msun
claims.finding: Outflow properties are significantly higher than survey values

evidence.quote: The estimated mass and momentum of the CO outflow are significantly higher than those estimated from surveys

claims.hypothesis: The outflow can disperse its core within the embedded phase
claims.experiment: Compared outflow and ambient mass distributions; estimated destruction timescale and efficiencies
claims.finding: Outflow can disperse the core and sets core-to-star efficiency

evidence.quote: the outflow is capable of dispersing the parent core within the typical lifetime of the embedded phase of a low-mass protostar

claims.hypothesis: Entrainment is by jet bow-shocks and/or a wide-angle wind
claims.experiment: Channel maps, PV diagrams, wind model, mass spectra
claims.result: Red cavity wall has nested shells; blue high-velocity gas fit by wind model
claims.finding: Both mechanisms co-exist on both sides

evidence.quote: we find evidence that jet bow-shock entrainment and wide-angle wind entrainment co-exist in both the blue-shifted and red-shifted outflows

claims.hypothesis: CS traces a rotating outflow entrained by a disk wind
claims.experiment: PV cuts perpendicular to CS jet-like structure
claims.result: Velocity gradients; j about 1600 AU km/s; launch radius about 60 AU
claims.finding: Tentative toroidal entrainment by disk wind from large radii

evidence.quote: We admit that this is only tentative evidence of outflow rotation.

limitations_admitted.value: Specific angular momentum is only an upper limit; envelope model is over-simplified; CO depletion neglected

evidence.quote: We note that the measured specific angular momentum is only an upper limit
the geometry or density/temperature distribution of the envelope in this model is over-simplified

reproducibility.score_reason: Data are public and the equations and adopted values are clear, but calibration/imaging details and masks are sparse and model fits are by eye.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Imaging settings and regions are underspecified, and several key results come from visual model fitting.
